trigger: an IdP serves only RSA keys under 2048 bits (a legacy or test IdP); the server is upgraded to this change
classification_rationale: the verify-time warning and Test Connection text did not mention the size floor, and upgrading.md and the fragment buried the break
summary: Reported as UP-1 by unhappy-path. Every key skipped leaves an empty key set and no sign-in succeeds (under --auth-mode=sso-only with no armed break-glass account, every operator is locked out); the parse-time warn names the reason but the verify-time warn and Test Connection did not. docs-writer F4 reported the same break hidden behind "Operator action: none" in the fragment.

Fixed in 3f3b515b4 and fc148427f: the verify-time warning (named kid and no-usable-key cases) says a key under the 2048-bit RSA floor is skipped at parse and points at the "failed to parse JWK" line; Test Connection's "no usable signing keys" text names the floor (asserted in test_settings_routes_oidc.cpp); upgrading.md has an entry with the sso-only break-glass caveat; the changelog fragment now leads with the operator action and no longer claims every mainstream IdP publishes 2048-bit keys (an assertion nothing in the repo supports). No escape-hatch flag was added (unhappy-path agreed: it would nullify the control); if wanted it is a separate issue (default 2048, audited, loud at boot). Rolling back restores the old behaviour (nothing is persisted).

trigger: a reader trusts the kMinRsaModulusBits comment that says the floor protects against a JWKS served by someone other than the IdP
classification_rationale: a party who controls the JWKS publishes its own 2048-bit key, so the floor does not defend that case

summary: Fixed in 3f3b515b4: the comment now says defence in depth against an IdP publishing a weak key and that it does not defend a tampered JWKS.

trigger: a no-kid token whose earlier published key parses but makes EVP_DigestVerifyInit fail
classification_rationale: the loop returned the first OpenSSL error and never tried the later keys
summary: Reported as F2 by security-guardian (unhappy-path UP-3 observed the same). Fails closed, IdP-controlled input, practically unreachable because only RSA keys parse.

Fixed in 3f3b515b4: the loop records the first error, continues to the next key, and returns that error only if no key verified the signature. No public trigger exists to test it (only RSA keys parse), which quality-engineer recorded as a residual.

trigger: a reader of the helper, evp_raii.hpp or the kid-refusal comment, or the thread that later reads the OpenSSL error queue
classification_rationale: stale or missing comments and up to 16 error-queue entries per no-kid token
summary: Batch: negative EVP_DigestVerifyFinal folded into false undocumented (cpp-safety), ERR_clear_error missing on a mismatch (cpp-safety, security-guardian F3), evp_raii.hpp says verify_jwt_signature frees its context by hand (cpp-safety, security-guardian F4, cpp-expert), "no-kid first-key path" comment (docs-writer F6, cpp-expert), inline constexpr in a named namespace of a .cpp (cpp-expert), resource ledger R1 said four frees instead of three and claimed nothing about TSan (cpp-safety).

Fixed in 3f3b515b4: ERR_clear_error() on a mismatch, the helper comment states the negative-result folding, the evp_raii.hpp and kid-refusal comments are corrected, the constants lose inline, the resource ledger says three frees and records that the new test cases are compiled out under TSan (ASan and UBSan run them).

trigger: a later edit moves kMinRsaModulusBits to any value from 1025 to 2047
classification_rationale: the cases pinned 1024 refused and 2048 kept only
summary: Reported as F1 by quality-engineer; also F3 (stale test name and comment saying a no-kid token uses the first key), F4 (the 17th-key refusal could pass on an unrelated error) and F5 (the new log text unpinned).

Fixed in 3f3b515b4: a 2047-bit key is refused by add_test_jwks_key and skipped by parse_jwks; the 17th-key refusal asserts the "signature verification failed" text; the log text "failed to parse JWK kid=... (RSA modulus under 2048 bits)" is pinned with a plain unparseable key shown to carry no size suffix; the stale test name and comment are reworded. MUTATION CHECK, run against the built binary: setting the floor to 2047 fails REQUIRE((*keys)->size() == 1) (test_oidc_provider.cpp:2265); earlier checks: candidate cap forced to 1 and floor forced to 1 each fail the new cases.

trigger: an operator diagnosing "token may be forged" for a no-kid token signed by a later key reads the troubleshooting row
classification_rationale: the row, the Deferred list and the log-line list still described the old first-key behaviour and listed #1901 as deferred
summary: Reported as F1, F2, F3, F5 by docs-writer (cpp-expert independently found the troubleshooting row). The merged #5962 fragment convention (bold Operator action lead) was not followed (F4).

Fixed in 3f3b515b4 and fc148427f: the troubleshooting row, the Deferred list, the "Log lines to watch" list (the failed-to-parse line and its size suffix), the "first 16 usable ones, in the order published" wording and the refusal consequence, the upgrading.md entry, the test-coverage.md row, and the changelog fragment lead.

trigger: a no-kid token against an IdP that publishes more than 16 usable keys and signs with the 17th or later
classification_rationale: the refusal says "may be forged" with no log that the key set was truncated
summary: Reported as UP-2 by unhappy-path. Not a regression (before, only the first key worked).
Fixed in 3f3b515b4: one warning per verification when a no-kid token meets more than 16 usable keys ("only the first 16 are tried").
